newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ job ads show strong rise in NZ in January.
newsitem.headline: NZ job ads show strong rise in NZ in January.

text.p: The number of job advertisements in newspapers rose sharply in January over the December level, with particularly strong growth in Auckland and Christchurch, according to the latest ANZ survey on Tuesday.
Nationally, the total number of job adverts in January rose 1 percent on a trend basis over the previous month but at 23,410 was down 5.6 percent on the January 1996 total of 24,787.
"While these results are encouraging, it is too early to say whether or not the trend toward stronger growth in job advertising will be sustained," the survey said.
"Several months of data will be required to establish whether the recent outcome marks a turning point in job advertising," the report added.
The monthly trend in Auckland showed a 0.9 percent rise in January to 17,604, compared with a 0.6 percent growth in December but was 4.3 percent lower than the 18,391 a year earlier.
For Christchurch, there was a 2.3 percent increase last month to 3612 but the level was 3.9 percent lower than the 3758 a year earlier.

In contrast, in Wellington, there was a 0.2 percent decline to 2195 ads in January, which was a slower decline than the 0.6 percent in December but left the total down 16.8 percent on the January 1996 total of 2637.

In the smaller regions, the actual change in the number of ads in January, compared with the December movement, showed Waikato up 16.4 percent (down 15.8 percent); Hawke's Bay down 2.0 percent (up 1.6 percent); Manawatu down 12.4 percent (down 13.4 percent); and Otago up 4.7 percent (down 14.1 percent).
